78908fd4e0a3: The Polish alphabet and the verb «to be»
1a5981ba00ba:
ę — pronounced like «en» inside a word and like «e» at the end of a word
kolęda (kolenda)
wędrować (vendrovach)
potężny (potenzhny)
woda – wodę (vode)
bluza – bluzę (blooze)
kurtka – kurtkę (kurtke)
2685822a085f:
ą — a nasal «o». Inside a word it is read like «on», at the end of a word like «ou»
Note: although the letter looks like «a», it is never read as «a»
wąż (vonzh)
mąż (monzh)
Śląsk (Shlonsk)
woda – wodą (vodou)
mama – mamą (mamou)
bluza – bluzą (bloozou)
0b67509684e4:
L — sounds like l
Lampa (lam-pa)
Latarka (la-tar-ka)
Ł — sounds like English w
ładny (wad-ny)
mały (ma-wy)
łatwy (wat-vy)
It is better to pronounce ł like English w and not like l — it will sound far more correct and natural.
06d65658929b:
C — sounds like ts in cats
Cena (tse-na)
cały (tsa-wy)
Cło (tswo)
S — sounds like s
Sens (sens)
Smaczny (smach-ny)
Słodki (swod-kee)
Z — sounds like z
Zamek (za-mek)
Zebra (zeb-ra)
Zmiana (zmya-na)
d08f9f63f22b:
CZ — sounds like a hard “ch”
Czas (chahs)
Człowiek (CHWO-vyek)
Czarny (CHAR-nih)
SZ — sounds like a hard “sh”
Szansa (SHAN-sah)
Szmatka (SHMAT-kah)
Szósty (SHOOS-tih)
SZCZ — sounds like “sh-ch”
Szczęście (SHCHEN-che)
3b819ec5bef3:
Ci — sounds like a soft “ch”
Ciemno (chyem-no)
Ciało (chya-wo)
Ciocia (cho-cha)
Si — sounds like a soft “sh”
Silny (sheel-ny)
Siny (shee-ny)
Osiem (o-shem)
Zi — sounds like a soft “zh”
Zima (zhee-ma)
Chodzić (kho-jeech)
Zielony (zhye-lo-ny)
d5dd47a70ccc:
The combination rz sounds different depending on the previous letter. After k, t, p, ch it sounds like “sh”, otherwise like “zh”.
As “sh”:
Krzaki (KSHA-kee)
Trzymać (TSHY-match)
Przykład (PSHIK-wad)
Chrzan (KHSHAN)
As “zh”:
Rzeka (ZHE-ka)
Korzeń (KO-zhen)
Burza (BOO-zha)
43d75a5ceee0:
Polish has two letters for the sound «kh»
Ch = H = [kh]
Chleb (khleb)
Chłopak (khwo-pak)
Chomik (kho-meek)
Hasło (khas-wo)
Herb (kherb)
Higiena (khee-gyen-a)
4431a162f384:
pan (sir, Mr) — about a man, polite “you”
pani (madam, Mrs) — about a woman, polite “you”
pan + pan = panowie (gentlemen) — they
pani + pani = panie (ladies) — they
pan + pani = państwo (ladies and gentlemen) — they
c589aa902331: oni — the masculine-personal group, that is, a group with at least one man in it.
12eb4cbf4710: one — the non-masculine-personal group, i.e. a group with no men in it. It can contain women, things or animals.
c6929decc367:
Czy jest cukierka? — Is there a sweet?
Czy są cukierki? — Are there sweets?
One item — jest, several — są.
